references.text: Jesus refers to himself as the one who has descended from heaven: 'No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man' (John 3:13). This is directly parallel to the expression 'the one who comes from heaven' in verse 31.

Jesus says: 'You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world' (John 8:23). The contrast between 'from above' (ἄνωθεν) and 'from below' / 'of the earth' precisely mirrors the same opposition found in 3:31.

'For the bread of God is he who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world' (John 6:33). Jesus as the one who comes from heaven is a recurring theme in the Gospel of John, parallel to 'the one who comes from above' in 3:31.
'I am the living bread that came down from heaven' (John 6:51). Jesus identifies himself as the one who has come down from heaven, directly consistent with 'the one who comes from heaven' in 3:31.

The testimony of John the Baptist: 'He who comes after me ranks before me, because he was before me' (John 1:15). John acknowledges Jesus' superior position, in line with the idea that the one who comes from above is 'over all' (3:31).
'The first man was of the earth, a man of dust; the second man is from heaven' (1 Cor 15:47). Paul uses the same contrast between the earthly and the heavenly as John does in 3:31.

'Then the Lord God formed the man of dust from the ground' (Gen 2:7). The expression 'the one who is of the earth' (ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς γῆς) in John 3:31 alludes to humanity's earthly origin as described in the creation account.
Paul describes Christ as 'God over all, blessed forever' (Rom 9:5). The expression 'over all' (ἐπὶ πάντων) reflects the Johannine 'ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν' and confirms Christ's sovereignty.
Christ is placed 'above all rule and authority, above every power and dominion' (Eph 1:21). This affirms the idea in John 3:31 that the one who comes from above is over all.

'Therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow' (Phil 2:9–10). Christ's exaltation above all things is a strong parallel to 'ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν' in John 3:31.

'He is before all things, and in him all things hold together. He is the head of the body, the church' (Col 1:17–18). Christ's preeminence over all creation underscores that he is 'over all', as proclaimed in John 3:31.
